inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if it does not. This is what happens when workers’ concerns are left unresolved for years: institutions can rely on their labor while delaying the commitments owed to them. Non-teaching staff deserve fair treatment, and the government should negotiate seriously rather than wait for workers to have to withdraw their labor to be heard.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to complete renegotiations of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, or face an indefinite nationwide strike. Workers should not have to threaten a shutdown to make institutions honor commitments they have left unresolved for years. Universities depend on non-teaching staff, yet their labor and livelihoods are too easily treated as secondary. The government needs to negotiate seriously and deliver fair treatment—not wait for workers to withdraw their labor before listening.
